item.title: Saturday, August 1, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: Monday August 3rd, Fannie and Freddie eliminate the limited condominium review, so every August condo closing now needs a full project review — call your condo contracts today, because New Jersey condo sales are already down eight point one percent year over year; the Fed's risk has flipped, holding nine to three with all three dissents in favour of a HIKE and CME FedWatch showing fifty seven point two percent odds of a September increase, so retire the wait-and-refinance pitch and call anyone with a lock expiring inside a fortnight; and New Jersey is loosening at the edges before it loosens on price, with inventory up four point nine percent, days on market out to forty one, and sale-to-list down to one hundred and one point three percent, so price new listings to actual comparable sales rather than to spring. Also inside: Freddie Mac at six point six six percent against a ten year Treasury of four point seven five, the United States weighing strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure with the Senate rejecting a war powers resolution fifty to forty nine, thirty four migrants drowned crossing to Ceuta, hyperscaler capital spending guided to three quarters of a trillion dollars for 2026, Spider-Man Brand New Day taking a record one hundred and sixty seven million dollars on opening day, and Real Madrid's seventy five million euro window under Mourinho.

item.title: Friday, July 31, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the FOMC held at three and a half to three and three quarters percent on a nine to three vote, with all three dissenters wanting a hike rather than a cut, so the wait-and-refinance pitch needs retiring; mind the gap between the Freddie Mac weekly survey at 6.66 percent and the daily tracker at 6.77 percent, because the daily number is the one clients get quoted; and Manhattan investment sales ran to ten billion dollars in the first half, up roughly fifty percent year over year with development sites up over fourteen hundred percent, so institutional capital has stopped waiting for cheaper debt. Also inside: Trump's announced Hamas disarmament deal, the Kyushu earthquake toll at thirty-four, Microsoft's record single-day market value gain against Meta's selloff, Sherrill and Mamdani on the local beat, and Real Madrid's eighty-million-euro approach for Rodri.

item.title: Thursday, July 30, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: Freddie Mac's weekly print lands at noon Eastern today and, after the Fed's divided hold and the bond sell-off that followed it, assume it goes up — call anyone with a rate lock expiring in the next fortnight before they read it elsewhere. Two: pending home sales fell five point four percent in June while Northeast inventory rose, so price new listings to actual comparable sales rather than to spring's optimism. Three: split your New York advice by product rather than by borough — luxury is surging on cash while co-ops stall on financing and board approval. And three things for the world. One: the Fed held at three point five zero to three point seven five percent, but three officials dissented in favour of a hike, so the debate is no longer about how fast rates come down. Two: southern Europe has evacuated more than three hundred and sixty thousand people and burned nearly three hundred thousand acres in a second heat wave at one hundred and seven Fahrenheit. Three: Spain are world champions, having beaten Argentina one nil at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

item.title: Wednesday, July 29, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the Fed decides this afternoon with no dot plot and markets pricing roughly a one-in-three chance of a HIKE rather than a cut, with the 10-year up 17bp in a month — rate-lock risk is asymmetric, so lock today; Freddie Mac prints tomorrow morning off a stale 6.58% while the daily tracker sits at 6.76%, so expect a jump toward the high 6.6s and brief clients before the headline lands; and the median new home has fallen below $400,000 to $398,300 against a 9.3-month new-home supply, so any resale seller competing with new construction needs repricing this week. And three things for the world: Iran fired ballistic missiles at US forces Tuesday (all intercepted) and the US and Saudi Arabia struck back jointly in Iraq for the first time, killing at least 20; southwest Europe has lost nearly 300,000 acres to wildfire with more than a third of a million people displaced; and the Senate advanced the late Lindsey Graham's Russia-Iran sanctions bill 86-12 on the day of his funeral, with President Zelensky in Washington. Also inside: Case-Shiller May at +1.1% year over year, Brooklyn medical office trading at $89.9m, Coca-Cola's beat, and Real Madrid 4-1 Leganes under Mourinho.

item.title: Tuesday, July 28, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the oil price collapse after the Iran ceasefire has taken the heat out of mortgage rates (30-year at 6.80%), but the Fed decides Wednesday at 2pm and the market is split roughly down the middle on hold versus hike — cuts are off the table entirely, so the risk of not locking is asymmetric; Fannie and Freddie eliminate the limited condo review on August 3rd, six days out, meaning every August condo closing needs a full review; and New Jersey has now seen over 10,800 announced job cuts this year, concentrated in Englewood Cliffs, Newark and Jersey City — watch those submarkets for autumn listing volume. And for the world: the US and Iran have stopped shooting but disagree publicly on whether talks exist; 330,000+ evacuated in the worst French and Spanish fire season on record; and Monday's chip selloff was about Chinese lithography advances, not AI spending.

item.title: Monday, July 27, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: mortgage rates hit a one-year high at roughly 6.75% with the Fed meeting Wednesday and the market pricing a hike rather than a cut; New Jersey is splitting by product type, with Essex single-family selling at 112% of list in 23 days while Hudson County condos sit at 42 days; and Fannie and Freddie eliminate limited condo reviews on August 3rd, adding an estimated $1,000+ per loan. Also today: New York State median price set a record at $475,000, Manhattan rents hit a record $5,295, landlords sued the NYC Rent Guidelines Board over the Mamdani rent freeze, US-Iran strikes paused for a second day, 300,000+ evacuated in French and Spanish wildfires, and Mourinho opened his second Real Madrid spell with a 1-0 win.
